summary: compute_check_digits lacks isinstance() guard and raises AttributeError (or TypeError for bytes) on non-string input; asymmetric with sibling validate() which returns False on the same inputs. Audit-deferred as 'defensive-coding only, fix in next patch'.
location: iban_pure/__init__.py:31-51 (compute_check_digits body, lines 32-33 specifically the missing guard before s.replace(...).upper())
repro: python -c 'from iban_pure import compute_check_digits; compute_check_digits(None)'   # AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'replace'
expected_vs_actual: expected=either return 2-digit check string OR raise the documented ValueError (per docstring: 'raises ValueError for strings shorter than 5 characters or containing non-alphanumeric characters'); actual=raises AttributeError on None/int/float/bool/tuple/list/dict/set and TypeError on bytes — neither documented nor symmetric with validate()
minimization_method: Manual — already 1-liner; verified to crash with no setup. Each of the 11 non-str inputs produces a distinct AttributeError/TypeError; the None case is the canonical minimal repro.
rationale: Audit card (cycle_67/01) explicitly DEFERRED this finding to the next patch cycle: 'defensive-coding only; not a security issue; no DoS; no data leak; cannot crash a host; only crashes a mis-wrapped try/except ValueError chain in the caller.' Fuzz run confirms: the 3 harnesses (1.7M iters) classified every compute_check_digits non-str raise as R5 'expected divergent behavior' (intentional counter), not as a regression. Slot-04 promotes M1 from audit-deferred to a tracked MEDIUM finding so it is not lost, but does NOT escalate to blocking — verdict remains compatible with SHIP pending a defensive follow-up patch in cycle_68.

summary: format_display strips whitespace/hyphens indiscriminately (mirrors validate behavior), so `format_display('DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00')` returns 'DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00' but `format_display(format_display(x))` round-trip is NOT invertible on already-spaced input from non-IBAN strings. Specifically: format_display of a non-IBAN-spaced string still produces 4-char groups, which may confuse downstream consumers expecting strict IBAN round-trip.
repro: python -c 'import iban_pure as ip; print(repr(ip.format_display("DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00")))'   # returns 'DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00' (round-trip ok)\npython -c 'import iban_pure as ip; print(repr(ip.format_display("DE89370400440532013000 extra garbage here")))'   # strips nothing because no whitespace, returns 'DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00 extra garbage here' (round-trip NOT invertible)
expected_vs_actual: expected=format_display should EITHER validate the IBAN first and raise ValueError on garbage, OR document that whitespace-stripping is its only normalization; actual=format_display silently formats ANY string (including garbage appendages) into 4-char groups without validating — caller cannot distinguish a valid formatted IBAN from a formatted garbage string
rationale: Audit-deferred; defensive-coding only; fuzz confirms format_display never raises on str input (zero raises across 500k iters).
